tools.name: azuremigrate_assessment_create
tools.description: Creates an Azure Migrate assessment: a datacenter (DC) migration proposal built from the on-premises inventory with the given target Azure region (location), currency and savings option. Returns the inventory summary, per-server Azure VM recommendations, on-premises vs Azure monthly cost and estimated savings. The request is authorized by the Azure Migrate Discovery Service as the signed-in user. POC: uses dummy inventory and illustrative prices.

location.description: Target Azure region for the migrated workloads, for example 'eastus', 'westeurope' or 'centralindia'.

currency.description: Currency for all cost figures. Valid values: 'USD', 'EUR', 'GBP', 'INR', 'JPY', 'AUD', 'CAD'. Defaults to 'USD'.

savings-option.description: Pricing commitment applied to Azure compute. Valid values: 'None' (pay-as-you-go), 'RI1Year', 'RI3Year' (reserved instances), 'ASP1Year', 'ASP3Year' (Azure savings plan). Defaults to 'RI3Year'.

assessment-name.description: Optional display name for the assessment. A name is generated when omitted.

tools.name: azuremigrate_upload_geturl
tools.description: Gets a URL to upload a file (for example a server inventory CSV or Excel file) to Azure Migrate. Call this when the user provides or attaches a file to import. Returns 'uploadUrl', a pre-authorized Azure Blob Storage SAS URL, plus the HTTP method and headers to use: upload the raw file bytes with an HTTP PUT to 'uploadUrl' and the header 'x-ms-blob-type: BlockBlob'. A 201 response means the upload succeeded. The URL is a temporary credential: do not show it to the user.

file-name.description: Name of the file the user wants to upload, including its extension, for example 'servers.csv' or 'inventory.xlsx'.

tools.name: azuremigrate_inventory_build
tools.description: Starts building an Azure Migrate server inventory from a file the user provides (for example a CMDB, CSV, Excel or zip export). Call this once per file when the user asks to build, import or discover an inventory. It creates a new Azure Migrate session for the signed-in user, starts the inventory build and returns 'uploadUrl', a pre-authorized Azure Blob Storage SAS URL: upload the raw file bytes with an HTTP PUT to 'uploadUrl' and the header 'x-ms-blob-type: BlockBlob'. HTTP 201 means the upload succeeded and the build runs in the background. Returns 'sessionId' and 'operationId' to reference the build. The URL is a temporary credential: do not show it to the user.

file-name.description: Name of the inventory file the user provided, including its extension, for example 'servers.csv', 'cmdb.xlsx' or 'export.zip'. Used only to describe the upload.

message.description: Optional instructions for the inventory build, for example 'only include production servers'. Omit when the user gave none.
